game: KC @ MIA, Week 3 2026, morning of kickoff; spread/total not saved; venue/rest/travel not in pack

script.base: No spread or total is saved, so the book’s lead/points answer is unknown and the script is inferred only from two-game form. KC’s skill volume (Kenneth Walker 47 car/290 rush yds and 16 tgt/79 rec yds; Travis Kelce 16 tgt/172 yds/85 air) against a Miami defense that blitzes 41% and allows 11.27 YPA in the middle, plus KC’s +0.36 EPA/dropback vs blitz (vs +0.10 with no blitz), points to a KC-leaning, competitive script: Walker stays in the 18–24 carry range if the game stays close or KC leads, Kelce works the middle, and Miami’s Malik Willis offense is capped by a -0.50 EPA/dropback vs blitz (KC blitzes 32%) and by KC allowing only 2 passes of 20+ on 63 attempts.
script.flip1: Miami hangs around or leads behind De’Von Achane (31 car/110, Wright doubtful) and KC’s Josh Simmons-less line cannot run. Walker’s pure rush stalls, Mahomes throws more, and Kelce/Rashee Rice/Xavier Worthy plus Walker checkdowns (he already has 16 targets) become the path — a pass-volume flip, not a Walker-off-the-field flip.
script.flip2: KC pulls away early and clocks it with Walker, or the reverse blowout if doubtful safety Chamarri Conner sits and Malik Washington (162 air yds) or Chris Bell hit the explosives KC has mostly prevented. Starters’ late snaps are then at risk, and Miami abandons the run so Achane’s 60.5 rush line dies while garbage targets leak to Bell/Kevin Coleman.

injury_fallout: Source: official pre-game nflverse injury report in the pack, plus weeks 1–2 usage. KC T Josh Simmons Out (back): pressure and rush-efficiency risk for Mahomes/Walker, more quick throws — gainers Kelce, Walker receiving, Emmett Johnson catches; loser deep yards (Worthy 82 air but only 43 rec yds). KC S Chamarri Conner Doubtful (knee): if he sits, Miami verticals (Washington, Bell) face a backup safety; not confirmed out on this morning report. MIA DE Rob Beal Jr. Out (hamstring): one edge rusher down, small pass-pro help for KC, not a named skill-player boost. MIA WR Caleb Douglas Out (ankle): vacates 10 tgt/113 yds/114 air; next men are Washington (already 13 tgt/96/162 air), Bell (3 tgt/25 yds), Coleman (2 tgt/0 yds), Greg Dulcich (5 tgt/35). Their saved lines are still ~50/50, so the absence is not visibly repriced. MIA RB Jaylen Wright Doubtful (stinger): Achane keeps the 31-carry lead; Ollie Gordon (3 car/7) and Willis (8 car/45) are the scraps. MIA WR Ryan Miller Questionable (hip) and CB Julius Brents Questionable (knee) are not outs; Brents sitting would help KC outside WRs more than Kelce. Final inactives (~90 min pre-kick) are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone chart in the pack (coverage charting missing). Proxy from Miami location splits over 2 games: middle 11.27 YPA on 15 att, left 8.09 on 22, right 6.67 on 15 — middle is the open area, not the boundary. KC shell proxy: middle 10.25 YPA but only 8 att, left 6.16 on 25, right 4.04 on 26, and only 2 of 63 passes went 20+.
matchup.pressure: Miami blitzes 41%. KC EPA/dropback is better vs blitz (+0.36) than vs no blitz (+0.10), so the blitz is not a Mahomes kill switch; it should increase RB/TE quick targets (Walker 16 tgt, Kelce 16 tgt, Johnson 4 tgt/64 yds on -12 air). KC blitzes 32% and Miami is bad vs blitz (-0.50 EPA/db vs +0.12 with none), which suppresses Miami’s deep air (Washington 162, Douglas was 114 and is out) more than it creates a clean Miami over.
matchup.bleeds: Miami bleeds the middle and allows explosives (6 passes of 20+ on 52 att; 6 runs of 10+). Rush YPC allowed is 3.95 — not a run bleed. KC bleeds the middle on a tiny sample (10.25 YPA, 8 att) but stuffs the right side (4.04) and explosives (2/63) and holds rushers to 3.93 YPC with 5 runs of 10+.
matchup.overlap: Kelce is the primary KC target (16 tgt, 85 air yards, not a pure checkdown) into the exact Miami soft spot (middle 11.27). Walker is the co-primary target and the carry engine into a 41% blitz that historically feeds RB catches, not into a weak run defense. Miami’s top option Washington is an air-yards receiver into a KC defense that has not given up explosives; that overlap fails, so he is not an edge despite Douglas’s vacated targets.

form: Avoiding season averages; only weeks 1–2 are in the pack (last4 columns are those two games). Walker rush 173 and 117 (both over 85.5), rush+rec 191 and 178 (both well over 109.5), rec 18 and 61 (splits 22.5). Kelce rec 71 and 101 (both over 52.5) on a team-high 16 targets. Worthy 18 and 25 on 13 targets/82 air — inefficient, do not fade or back. Rice 19 and 83 — one-play volatile vs 48.5. Thornton 0 and 86 vs 18.5 — boom/bust. Johnson rush 24 and 15 (both under 26.5) behind Walker’s 47 carries; his rec 44 and 20 both cleared 10.5, so the under there is dead. Achane rush 36 and 74 vs 60.5, rush+rec 66 and 93 vs 93 (no price). Washington 53 and 43 vs 40.5 but the KC explosive suppression is the form-vs-matchup conflict. Dulcich 18 and 17 vs 22.5. No prior-opponent labels, so these yards are not defense-adjusted.

data_check.notes: Step 8 is incomplete: no projection, no sims, no Pinnacle. model_p values are heuristics from the two-game role versus the line, kept under 0.70 because past calibration in the skill warns that 70–80% ratings hit near 50%. Form agrees with both legs (Kelce 71/101 vs 52.5; Walker 191/178 vs 109.5). The counter-data is matchup, not a model: Miami 3.95 YPC and Simmons Out argue Walker’s 6.17 YPC will not repeat. Applying 3.95 YPC to ~22 carries is ~87 rush yards, and his 79 receiving yards over two games are ~40 per game, so a regressed rush+rec still projects near or over 109.5 — not a hard disagree. No-vig is a coin flip, so the market has not priced the role. Disagree-on-a-lean rule is not triggered hard enough to drop Walker; it is flagged for the human. No leg was cut by averages.

pre_mortem: It’s Monday and both lost. Miami played two-high and bracketed Kelce, so the middle 11.27 YPA never showed up in his routes; Worthy and Rice took the six-explosive tendency and Kelce finished in the mid-30s on 5 targets. At the same time Simmons’s absence turned Walker’s runs into 3.5-yard stuffs, KC fell behind, Walker was pulled late, and Johnson vultured the hurry-up carries — Walker ended around 55 rush and 15 receiving, under 109.5. The two-game 191/178 sample was opponent-driven (opponents not in the pack) and the coin-flip price was the sharp side. A second loss path is weather we do not have: 15+ mph wind or rain would cut Kelce’s 85 air yards and help a lower-event game neither over needs. If that counter-case is right, the human should pass both; the read still prefers the overs because Miami has blitzed 41% and has not shown it can take the middle away.
slip_story: One story only: KC skill usage versus a blitz-heavy, middle-soft Miami defense. Stack is Kelce recyds over with Walker rush+rec over. They win together if KC moves the ball either by running or by checking down. Do not add Miami unders, a game under (total unknown), Mahomes rush over (that needs him to hold the ball, which fights the quick-throw Kelce path), or Washington/Bell overs (those need the flip where KC’s explosive suppression fails). Two legs, no TDs, no depth receivers. Not a bet — candidate only.
